hook: The prime minister who refused to give in to Hitler, and led Britain through the Second World War.

pages.x: Winston Churchill was born in 1874 at Blenheim Palace, the son of a politician and an American heiress. He did badly at school, and failed the army entrance exam twice before he got in.

As a war reporter in South Africa in 1899 he was captured by the Boers. He escaped from a prison camp in Pretoria, hid in a coal mine and on a goods train, and reached safety. It made him a hero at home.
In the First World War, as head of the navy, he backed the attack on Gallipoli in 1915, a disaster that cost many lives. He resigned and went to fight in the trenches.
In the 1930s, out of office, he warned again and again that Hitler's Germany was arming for war. Few listened. He painted, laid bricks in his garden at Chartwell, and wrote.

In May 1940, as France fell, he became prime minister: "I have nothing to offer but blood, toil, tears and sweat." "We shall fight on the beaches... we shall never surrender." For a year Britain fought on alone.
pages.img: We shall fight on the beaches

pages.x: He worked with Roosevelt and Stalin, meeting them at Tehran and Yalta, and led Britain to victory in 1945. Weeks later, voters threw him out in a general election.
In 1946, in Missouri, he warned that "an iron curtain has descended across the continent" of Europe, the start of the Cold War.
His views on empire and race were harsh even for his time. He bitterly opposed independence for India, and many blame his government's choices for making the Bengal famine of 1943 worse.
Prime minister again from 1951 to 1955, he won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953 for his histories and speeches. When he died in 1965, he was given a state funeral.
Churchill led Britain through its darkest hour, refusing to make peace with Hitler, and his speeches still stir people today.

Refused to make peace with Hitler in 1940
Won the Nobel Prize in Literature
